implementation_statement: Group POL-02 Access Control Policy applies; the Hydro supplement adds OT rules (separate OT identity domain, Intermediate Systems, vendor sessions). CIP-003-9 R1 policies are reviewed and approved by the CIP Senior Manager every 15 calendar months.
evidence: POL-02; Hydro supplement; CIP-003 policy approval record 2026-02-24
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R03 (CIP-003-9 R1); C-DAMS-R01 (Rev. 3A Table 9.3a access control)

implementation_statement: OT accounts live in the OT identity domain, not SYS-G1. HR joiner, mover, and leaver events from SYS-G4 feed a ticket to the OT security team. Named accounts only at the HOCs; account types and approvers are defined in the OT account standard.
evidence: OT account standard; OT domain export; ticket sample
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R03 (CIP-004-7 R4 Part 4.1); C-DAMS-R01 (Table 9.3b access control)

implementation_statement: OT PAM automates account creation, disabling after 35 days of inactivity, and quarterly certification campaigns for HOC and plant accounts.

control_name: Automated Temporary and Emergency Account Management
implementation_statement: Temporary and emergency OT accounts expire automatically after 72 hours.
OT accounts are disabled after 35 days of inactivity; service accounts are exempt by documented exception with owner review.
Account creation, modification, enabling, disabling, and removal in the OT domain and OT PAM are logged and forwarded to the group SIEM.
evidence: SIEM saved search; OT PAM audit log

implementation_statement: HOC consoles lock after 15 minutes idle where the operator display allows; operator consoles that must stay visible use a supervised shared display mode inside the PSP with individual sign-in for commands.
Gate and unit command privileges at the HOC are usable only from consoles inside the HOC PSPs.

The group SOC alerts on atypical OT PAM use at the HOCs. Gap: plant HMIs at 27 of 41 plants have no account monitoring, and Constructors commissioning accounts at plants were not monitored at all (gap 1).
evidence: SOC use case list; DEV-05 finding 2026-07-15

implementation_statement: High-risk users (termination for cause, credential compromise) are disabled in OT PAM within 1 hour of the SOC or HR notice.
Role-based access in SCADA, HMIs, and OT PAM: viewer, operator, supervisor, engineer, and administrator roles; gate and unit commands require operator role or higher.

Flows between OT zones and to the OT DMZ are allow-listed at the HOC ESP firewalls and plant gateway firewalls. Gap: 17 plants send historian data to the DSMS by two-way replication instead of a one-way diode (gap 3).
evidence: Firewall rule review 2026-06; DSMS data flow diagram
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Table 9.3a access control and functional segregation); C-DAMS-R03 (CIP-005-7 R1 Part 1.3)

implementation_statement: Separation of duties: OT engineers cannot approve their own changes; operators cannot change PLC logic; OT PAM administrators cannot approve their own access.
Least privilege by role; engineering privileges granted per task through OT PAM.
Security functions (firewall rules, OT PAM, sensor configuration) are restricted to the OT security team.
Administrators use separate non-privileged accounts for e-mail and web, which are not reachable from OT.
Privileged OT accounts are vaulted in OT PAM; checkout requires a ticket and MFA, and sessions are recorded.
Privileges for user role categories are reviewed every 15 calendar months; last review 2026-03.
Privileged functions are logged in OT PAM and the SCADA event journal.

control_name: Prohibit Non-privileged Users from Executing Privileged Functions
implementation_statement: Operator accounts cannot run engineering or administrative functions in SCADA.
HOC SCADA and Intermediate Systems lock after 5 failed attempts; plant HMIs that cannot lock generate an alert in SCADA after 5 failures.
Intermediate Systems and HMIs show a notice of authorized use and monitoring.
Engineering workstations lock after 15 minutes; operator consoles follow AC-2(5).
Remote sessions through the Intermediate Systems end after 30 minutes idle and 8 hours maximum.

control_name: Permitted Actions Without Identification or Authentication
implementation_statement: No actions are permitted without identification, except read-only overview displays in the HOC control room inside the PSP.

All Interactive Remote Access to the HOC ESPs uses Intermediate Systems with MFA and encryption. Gap: Constructors commissioning kits connected directly to plant and gate control networks over cellular routers at rehabilitation sites (gap 1). Interim rule from 2026-07-16: escorted, scheduled sessions only.
evidence: Intermediate System design; DEV-05 finding; interim rule memo
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R03 (CIP-005-7 R2 Parts 2.1-2.3; CIP-003-9 Att. 1 Sec. 3.1 and 6); C-DAMS-R01 (Form 3 Q12)

implementation_statement: Remote sessions through the Intermediate Systems are logged and reviewed by the SOC. Gap: sessions through commissioning kits were invisible to monitoring.

control_name: Protection of Confidentiality and Integrity Using Encryption
implementation_statement: Remote access sessions are encrypted to the Intermediate Systems.
Remote access is routed through 2 Intermediate System clusters (one per HOC).
Privileged commands over remote access are allowed only for named engineers with an approved change ticket; gate and unit commands are never allowed remotely except from HOC consoles.
Wireless is prohibited inside the HOC ESPs. Plant wireless (gauge links) is evaluated before use and kept outside control zones.
Mobile devices may not connect to OT networks; operator phones are used only for voice and the paging system.
Only Hydro-managed transient devices may connect to OT. Gap: Constructors and OEM laptops connected during commissioning without the CIP-003-9 Attachment 1 Section 5.2 review (gap 1).
evidence: Transient Cyber Asset log; DEV-05 finding

implementation_statement: Sharing of BCSI and security-sensitive documents requires owner approval and an NDA; CEII rules apply.
Group POL-05 and the training standard apply; the Hydro supplement adds OT role-based training.
Annual security awareness for all workforce; quarterly CIP security awareness reinforcement for people with authorized access to the HOC BES Cyber Systems.
evidence: Training completion report 2026; quarterly awareness records
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R03 (CIP-004-7 R1 Part 1.1; CIP-003-9 Att. 1 Sec. 1)

implementation_statement: Insider threat module in annual training, including OT scenarios.
Social engineering training with quarterly phishing exercises for all corporate users, including HOC staff.
CIP training (CIP-004-7 R2) is completed before access and every 15 calendar months. Gap: Constructors commissioning engineers who work in plant control networks receive no OT role-based training.
evidence: CIP training records; Constructors training matrix

implementation_statement: Training records are kept for 6 years in the training platform.
Logged event types: successful and failed logins, privileged actions, malicious code detections, gate and unit commands, and setpoint and logic changes.
Records include time, source, user, event type, and outcome.
Log collectors at each HOC hold 180 days; plants buffer 30 days.

control_name: Response to Audit Logging Process Failures
implementation_statement: Logging failures generate alerts to the SOC.

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: The SOC reviews HOC logs continuously and summaries every 15 days. Gap: plants without sensors have only firewall logs, reviewed weekly.
Automated correlation in the SIEM.
OT logs are correlated with corporate identity, EDR, and physical access events.
OT time comes from GPS clocks at each HOC and plant.
Logs are forwarded to the SIEM, which operators and engineers cannot alter.
HOC event logs kept at least 90 consecutive calendar days on site and 1 year in the SIEM.
Audit generation is enabled on SCADA servers, Intermediate Systems, firewalls, and OT PAM.
Group assessment policy; group internal audit charter.
Group internal audit with a co-sourced OT firm assesses this system each year (P07); SERC audits the CIP program.
Assessors are independent of Hydro operations and of the OT security team.
Interconnection agreements exist for the 3 Balancing Authority ICCP links. Gap: no agreement covers the DSMS connection or Constructors commissioning connections.
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R03 (CIP-012-2 R1 Part 1.5); C-DAMS-R01 (Table 9.3a network connections)

implementation_statement: The group POA&M tracks every weakness (P07); Section 9 negative answers are sent to the Regional Engineers as plans and schedules.
Authorized to operate with conditions on 2026-09-10 (SSP section 4.2).
Continuous monitoring at the HOCs; plant monitoring is partial (14 of 41 plants with sensors).
Penetration test of the HOC ESP perimeters every 2 years by an outside firm; last 2025-10.
Internal connections between HOC zones are documented and approved.
Group configuration management standard; Hydro supplement for OT changes.
Baselines (operating system, software, ports, patches) exist for HOC BES Cyber Systems. Gap: plant baselines are complete for 29 of 41 plants.
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R03 (CIP-010-4 R1 Part 1.1); C-DAMS-R01 (Table 9.3a system lifecycle)

implementation_statement: Changes to HOC systems are authorized and documented with a CIP-010 security impact step. Gap: rehabilitation projects changed gate PLCs at 2 plants under Constructors change records, not Hydro's.
Security impact analysis before each change to the HOC systems (CIP-010-4 Part 1.4).
Only OT engineers in OT PAM can change logic and configurations.
Hardening settings from vendor guides are applied to HOC servers and Intermediate Systems.
Only needed logical ports and services are enabled; physical ports on HOC consoles are blocked.
Application allow-listing on plant HMIs is planned with the HMI replacement program (2027).
Inventory of cyber assets with Section 9 criticality for HOCs and plants. Gap: transient devices and commissioning kits are not in the inventory, and 3 plants have unverified device lists.
Inventory is updated with each change and each new asset.
OT configuration management plan covers HOC and plant systems.
Software licenses tracked by group procurement.
Users cannot install software on OT hosts.
Group continuity policy; Hydro supplement for OT recovery.
CIP-009 recovery plans for HOC systems; plant recovery procedures; Rapid Recovery sub-elements in the Group 1 Security Plans.
Recovery plans are coordinated with the EAPs and the Transmission Operators' restoration plans.
Gate and dam safety functions resume first (local control within 1 hour).
Critical assets identified from the BIA (P05).
Operators drill local gate and unit control each year; HOC staff train on failover.
Recovery plans tested every 15 calendar months; HOC failover tested 2026-06-13. Gap: failover took 2.6 hours against a 2-hour RTO.
Backups stored at the other HOC and in offline media.
HOC-B is the alternate site, about 170 miles from HOC-A.
Diverse telecom: licensed microwave plus leased circuits from 2 carriers to each HOC.
SCADA backups nightly with offline copies. Gap: PLC logic backups at 12 plants are more than 12 months old.
Recovery to a known state for HOC systems; plant recovery depends on stale backups at 12 plants.
Group identification and authentication standard; OT domain rules in the Hydro supplement.
Unique user identification in the OT domain; no shared accounts at the HOCs.
MFA for privileged access via OT PAM.
MFA for remote non-privileged access through the Intermediate Systems.
Replay-resistant authentication (hardware tokens) for OT PAM.
Device authentication for plant gateways and ICCP peers.
Identifiers assigned on approval and not reused for 2 years.

Password parameters per CIP-007-6 Part 5.5; vendor defaults changed at commissioning. Gap: 6 plant HMIs still use generic local accounts (inventoried under CIP-007-6 Part 5.2) and the DEV-05 commissioning router had a default password.
Non-organizational users (vendors) authenticate through vendor accounts in OT PAM.
Re-authentication for privileged checkout every session.
Group POL-03; Hydro supplement adds OT and dam safety steps (EAP link).
Incident roles trained; HOC supervisors trained on CIP-008 determinations.
CIP-008 plan tested every 15 calendar months (last 2026-03 tabletop). Gap: no exercise has included another division or the disclosure committee.
SOC handles incidents with OT playbooks (P08). Gap: cross-division incidents have no single incident commander rule.
Automated case management in the SOC platform.
Incidents tracked and documented in the SOC case system.
Reporting to E-ISAC and CISA (CIP-008-6 R4), the FERC Regional Engineer (18 CFR 12.10), and DOE-417 when required. Gap: the multi-regulator matrix (P08) has not been exercised.
SOC and retainer firm provide response help.
The CIP-008 plan and the P08 runbook; EAP cross-references.
Group maintenance standard; Hydro supplement for OT maintenance.
Controlled maintenance with work orders in the enterprise asset management system.
Nonlocal maintenance only through the Intermediate Systems with recording. Gap: OEM and Constructors maintenance through commissioning kits bypassed this path.
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R03 (CIP-005-7 R2 Parts 2.4-2.5; CIP-003-9 Att. 1 Sec. 6)

implementation_statement: Maintenance personnel without authorized access are escorted inside PSPs and plant control rooms.
Group media protection standard.
OT media sanitized or destroyed before reuse or disposal.
Removable media scanned at kiosks at the HOCs and 30 plants. Gap: 11 plants have no kiosk; contractors bring their own media.
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R03 (CIP-003-9 Att. 1 Sec. 5.3; CIP-010-4 R4); C-DAMS-R01 (Form 3 Q17)

implementation_statement: Hydro physical security program and Security Plans.
Authorized access lists for HOC PSPs and plant control rooms.
Card access and guards at HOCs; locks and cameras at plants and gate houses.
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R03 (CIP-006-6 R1 Part 1.2; CIP-003-9 Att. 1 Sec. 2)

implementation_statement: PSP access monitored with alarms to security dispatch within 15 minutes.
Visitor logs kept at least 90 calendar days.
Uninterruptible power and standby generators for HOCs and gate control.
Group planning policy.
This SSP and the fleet Cyber/SCADA Security Plan. Gap: the Cyber/SCADA plan does not cover construction connections or the DSMS path.
Rules of behavior in POL-05 with the OT addendum.
Zoned architecture (HOC ESP, plant control, dam safety zone, DMZ).
Group personnel security standard.
Personnel risk assessments with 7-year criminal history checks before access and every 7 years.
Termination events reach the OT security team the same day; access removed within 24 hours.
Transfers reviewed and unneeded access removed by the next calendar day.

Vendor PRAs verified for people with authorized access (CIP-004-7 Part 3.4). Gap: Constructors commissioning staff at plants are not covered by the external personnel rules because they are affiliates.
Group risk policy (POL-01 4.3).
FIPS 199 categorization (SSP section 6) and Section 9 criticality determinations (2026-07-08).
Annual risk assessment rolled into the group register (P01).
Paper or active vulnerability assessments at the HOCs every 15 calendar months (CIP-010-4 R3). Gap: 15 of 41 plants without an OT vulnerability assessment in the last 12 months (Table 9.3b).

implementation_statement: Critical components identified in the Section 9 inventory.
OT contracts include security terms from the CIP-013 plan. Gap: the 2025 renewal with the governor and excitation OEM skipped them.
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R03 (CIP-013-2 R1 Part 1.2; R2); C-DAMS-R01 (Table 9.3a acquisition standards)

implementation_statement: Security design review for new OT systems and modifications.
Service providers with OT access are reviewed in the third-party program. Gap: Engineering (DSMS) and Constructors (commissioning) are not treated as service providers.
Unsupported components tracked: 58 plant HMIs and 11 gate control workstations; replacement funded for 2027.
Group system and communications protection standard.
Rate limits on DMZ services; HOC ESP firewalls protect against floods.
Electronic Security Perimeters at both HOCs with Electronic Access Points; plant gateway firewalls. Gap: the two-way DSMS path at 17 plants and commissioning kits at rehabilitation sites.
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R03 (CIP-005-7 R1 Parts 1.1-1.3; CIP-003-9 Att. 1 Sec. 3.1); C-DAMS-R01 (Table 9.3a segregation)

implementation_statement: Limited access points to OT (2 HOC EAPs and one gateway per plant).
External telecom services documented with interface rules.

control_name: Deny by Default — Allow by Exception
implementation_statement: Deny by default, allow by exception at every EAP.
Split tunneling disabled for remote access.
ICCP and inter-HOC links encrypted.
Cryptographic protection on ICCP links.
Keys for OT certificates managed in the OT PKI.
Backups and BCSI repositories encrypted.
Process isolation provided by vendor platforms.
Group system integrity standard.
Patch sources tracked and evaluated every 35 calendar days with mitigation plans. Gap: 58 HMIs and 11 gate workstations cannot be patched (unsupported).
Malicious code protection on HOC servers and Intermediate Systems; signatures updated through the OT update server. Gap: commissioning kits and some plant HMIs had no protection.
Passive OT sensors at both HOCs and 14 of 41 plants, monitored 24x7 by the SOC. Gap: 27 plants without sensors.

control_name: Automated Tools and Mechanisms for Real-time Analysis
implementation_statement: Automated real-time analysis at all HOC-operated plants planned with the sensor rollout (2027-06-30).
Inbound and outbound traffic monitored at HOC EAPs. Gap: plant gateways and DSMS paths only partly monitored.
CISA ICS advisories, E-ISAC, and vendor alerts reviewed daily.
Software integrity verified before install (CIP-010-4 Part 1.6).
Periodic integrity checks of PLC logic against offline copies planned from 2027-03.
Records kept per the group retention schedule and NERC evidence retention rules.
Group supply chain policy and the CIP-013 plan.
CIP-013 plan reviewed and approved every 15 calendar months (last 2026-01).
Supply chain controls in OT procurement. Gap: OEM concentration (55% of units) and the skipped CIP-013 terms.
Acquisition strategies favor vendors with incident notification and vulnerability disclosure terms.
Supplier assessments for tier 1 OT vendors. Gap: Constructors and Engineering are not assessed as suppliers to Hydro.
Components bought from OEMs or authorized resellers only.
